message.content: What was NVIDIA's initial focus in computing?|PC graphics.|NVIDIA pioneered accelerated computing to help solve the most challenging computational problems. Starting with a focus on PC graphics, we extended our focus in recent years to the revolutionary field of artificial intelligence, or AI.

What technology did NVIDIA leverage to create platforms for VR, HPC, and AI?|GPU architecture.|Fueled by the sustained demand for exceptional 3D graphics and the scale of the gaming market, NVIDIA leveraged its GPU architecture to create platforms for virtual reality, or VR, high performance computing, or HPC, and AI.

What is the role of NVIDIA's GPU in deep learning?|NVIDIA's GPU simulates human intelligence, enabling a deeper understanding of the physical world and running deep learning algorithms.|The GPU was initially used to simulate human imagination, enabling the virtual worlds of video games and films. Today, it also simulates human intelligence, enabling a deeper understanding of the physical world. Its parallel processing capabilities, supported by up to thousands of computing cores, are essential to running deep learning algorithms.

How many applications do NVIDIA GPUs support?|Over 600 applications.|With support for more than over 600 applications - including the top 15 HPC applications - NVIDIA GPUs enable some of the most promising areas of discovery, from weather prediction to materials science and from wind tunnel simulation to genomics.

Which countries house the top supercomputers powered by NVIDIA GPUs located outside the United States?|Europe and Japan.|NVIDIA GPUs power the top two supercomputers in the world, located at Oak Ridge and Lawrence Livermore National Laboratories in the United States, as well as the top supercomputers in Europe and Japan.
What are NVIDIA's two main reportable segments?|GPU and Tegra Processor.|Our Businesses Our two reportable segments - GPU and Tegra Processor - are based on a single underlying architecture.

What does NVIDIA's Tegra brand integrate?|An entire computer onto a single chip, incorporating GPUs and multi-core CPUs.|Our Tegra brand integrates an entire computer onto a single chip, and incorporates GPUs and multi-core CPUs to drive supercomputing for autonomous robots, drones, and cars, as well as for game consoles and mobile gaming and entertainment devices.

What GPU product brands target AI data scientists and big data researchers?|Tesla and DGX|Our GPU product brands are aimed at specialized markets including GeForce for gamers; Quadro for designers; Tesla and DGX for AI data scientists and big data researchers; and GRID for cloud-based visual computing users.

What is the primary design purpose of Tegra processors?|To enable branded platforms such as AGX and SHIELD.|Tegra Processor | ∙ | Tegra processors are primarily designed to enable branded platforms - AGX and SHIELD

Which NVIDIA platform is designed for AI computing in self-driving vehicles?|DRIVE AGX|AGX is a power-efficient AI computing platform for intelligent edge devices, including: | | - DRIVE AGX for self-driving vehicles

What technology did NVIDIA develop for real-time cinematic-quality rendering?|RTX ray tracing technology|We developed NVIDIA RTX ray tracing technology to enable real-time, cinematic-quality rendering in the RTX line-up of our gaming platforms.

Which markets does NVIDIA specialize in with its GPU-based visual computing and accelerated computing platforms?|Gaming, Professional Visualization, Data Center, and Automotive|From our proprietary processors, we created platforms that address four large markets where our expertise is critical: Gaming, Professional Visualization, Data Center, and Automotive.

How do NVIDIA GPUs enhance the gaming experience?|By improving visual quality of graphics, increasing frame rates for smoother gameplay, and improving realism through the behavior of light and physical objects.|Our GPUs enhance the gaming experience by improving the visual quality of graphics, increasing the frame rate for smoother gameplay and improving realism by incorporating the behavior of light and physical objects.

What does VRWorks software provide for developers?|VRWorks allows developers to create fully immersive experiences by enabling physically realistic visuals, sound, touch interactions, and simulated environments.|To enable VR, we provide developers with a suite of software libraries called VRWorks. VRWorks allows developers to create fully immersive experiences by enabling physically realistic visuals, sound, touch interactions, and simulated environments.

What platform did NVIDIA introduce in fiscal year 2019 for rendering photorealistic objects?|NVIDIA RTX platform|During fiscal year 2019, we introduced the NVIDIA RTX platform, making it possible to render film-quality, photorealistic objects and environments with physically accurate shadows, reflections and refractions using ray tracing in real-time.

What are some enterprise applications incorporating VR technology as mentioned in the text?|Virtual car showrooms, surgical training, architectural walkthroughs, and bringing historical scenes to life|Just as VR is becoming more important in gaming, it is also being incorporated in a growing number of enterprise applications, including within medicine, architecture, product design, and retail. Virtual car showrooms, surgical training, architectural walkthroughs, and bringing historical scenes to life all deploy this technology, powered by our GPUs.

What is the brand name for NVIDIA's market aimed at professionals needing high performance graphics?|Quadro|Our brand for this market is Quadro for workstations. Quadro GPUs enhance the productivity of designers by improving performance and adding functionality, such as photorealistic rendering, high color fidelity, and advanced scalable display capabilities.

Which industries are mentioned as using NVIDIA's AI platform for automating tasks and enhancing services?|Healthcare, financial services, and oil exploration|We are engaged with thousands of organizations working on AI in a multitude of industries, from automating tasks such as reading medical images, to enabling fraud detection in financial services, to optimizing oil exploration and drilling.

Which major cloud services companies are using AI for applications like voice recognition and real-time translation?|Amazon, Baidu, and Facebook|These organizations include the world’s leading cloud services companies such as Amazon, Baidu, and Facebook, which are infusing AI in applications that enable highly accurate voice recognition and real-time translation.

Cisco, Dell, HP|To enable deep learning and machine learning, we provide a family of GPUs designed to speed up training and inferencing of neural networks. They are available in industry standard servers from every major computer maker worldwide, including Cisco, Dell, HP, Inspur, and Lenovo.

What is one area where GPUs have significantly impacted scientific discovery?|Improving heart surgery|GPUs have significantly impacted scientific discovery, including improving heart surgery, mapping human genome folds, seismic modeling, and weather simulations.

How have GPUs contributed to scientific discovery?|GPUs have significantly impacted scientific discovery by improving heart surgery, mapping human genome folds, seismic modeling, and weather simulations.|GPUs have significantly impacted scientific discovery, including improving heart surgery, mapping human genome folds, seismic modeling, and weather simulations.

Why is accelerated computing considered important for the future of computing?|Accelerated computing is considered important due to the slowing of Moore’s Law and is seen as the path forward for computing.|Accelerated computing is recognized as the path forward for computing amid the slowing of Moore’s Law.

What role does Tesla GPU accelerators play in the world's fastest supercomputers?|Tesla GPU accelerators power many of the world's fastest supercomputers, including the Summit and Sierra in the U.S., Piz Daint in Europe, ABCI in Japan, and the supercomputer by Eni in Italy.|Tesla GPU accelerators power many of the world’s fastest supercomputers, including the U.S. Department of Energy’s Summit and Sierra supercomputers at Oak Ridge and Lawrence Livermore National Laboratories, Europe’s fastest supercomputer - Piz Daint - in Switzerland, Japan’s fastest supercomputer, ABCI; and the world’s fastest industrial supercomputer by Italian energy company Eni.

What applications does GRID enable in data centers?|GRID enables the running of graphics-intensive applications remotely on a server in the data center, accelerating virtual desktop infrastructures and delivering graphics-intensive applications from the cloud for industries such as manufacturing, healthcare, and educational institutions.|GRID makes it possible to run graphics-intensive applications remotely on a server in the data center. Applications include accelerating virtual desktop infrastructures and delivering graphics-intensive applications from the cloud for industries such as manufacturing, healthcare, and educational institutions, among others.

What are the key components of NVIDIA's DRIVE platform?|NVIDIA's DRIVE platform includes the high-performance, energy-efficient hardware DRIVE AGX, and open, modular software such as DRIVE AV for autonomous driving and DRIVE IX for in-vehicle AI assistance.|NVIDIA DRIVE computing platform. The platform consists of high-performance, energy efficient hardware - DRIVE AGX, and open, modular software - including DRIVE AV for autonomous driving and DRIVE IX for in-vehicle AI assistance.

What functionality does the DRIVE AutoPilot provide in NVIDIA's automotive solutions?|The DRIVE AutoPilot powers NVIDIA's Level 2+ automated driving solution, combining the DRIVE AV self-driving solution with the DRIVE IX cockpit software, allowing the driver to visualize what the car sees and plans to do.|It powers the DRIVE AutoPilot, NVIDIA’s Level 2+ automated driving solution, combining the DRIVE AV self-driving solution with the DRIVE IX cockpit software, including a visualization system for allowing the driver to see what the car sees and plans to do.

How does NVIDIA's strategy leverage its GPU architecture across different market platforms?|NVIDIA's strategy leverages its GPU architecture across diverse market platforms by using a unified architecture based on GPUs and CUDA, allowing for leveraged investments in R&D to support multi-billion dollar markets like Gaming, Professional Visualization, Data Center, and Automotive.|Advancing the GPU computing platform. GPUs can help solve problems that were previously deemed unsolvable. We work to deliver continued GPU performance leaps that outpace Moore’s Law by leveraging innovation across the architecture, chip design, system, and software layers. Our strategy is to target markets where GPUs deliver order-of-magnitude performance advantages relative to legacy approaches. Our market platforms so far include Gaming, Professional Visualization, Data Center, and Automotive. While  the requirements of these end markets are diverse, we address them with a unified underlying architecture leveraging our GPUs and CUDA as the fundamental building blocks.

What market platforms does the company include in its operations?|Gaming, Professional Visualization, Data Center, and Automotive|Our market platforms so far include Gaming, Professional Visualization, Data Center, and Automotive.

How does the company's programmable architecture benefit its R&D investments?|It allows support for multi-billion dollar end markets using the same technology through various software stacks either developed internally or by third parties.|The programmable nature of our architecture allows us to make leveraged investments in R&D: we can support several multi-billion dollar end markets with the same underlying technology by using a variety of software stacks developed either internally or by third party developers and partners.

What components are included in the company's GPU computing platform for AI?|GPUs, CUDA programming language, algorithms, libraries, and system software|We provide a complete, end-to-end GPU computing platform for deep learning and machine learning, addressing both training and inferencing. This includes GPUs, our CUDA programming language, algorithms, libraries, and system software.

How does the company intend to expand its AI technology leadership?|By adding AI-specific features to its GPU architecture and leveraging a large and expanding ecosystem.|GPUs are uniquely suited to AI, and we will continue to add AI-specific features to our GPU architecture to further extend our leadership position. Our AI technology leadership is reinforced by our large and expanding ecosystem in a virtuous cycle.

What is the company's approach to gaming and visual computing markets?|Enhancing user experiences through libraries and algorithms for cinematic and VR experiences, optimizing gaming on GeForce, and enabling cloud platform access.|Our technologies are instrumental in driving gaming forward, as developers leverage our libraries and algorithms to create near-cinematic and VR experiences. Our close collaboration with game developers allows us to deliver an optimized gaming experience on our GeForce platform.

What solution does the company provide for the autonomous vehicle market?|A full functionally safe AI-based hardware and software solution under the DRIVE brand, including GPU-based hardware for neural network training and operation re-simulation.|We provided a full functionally safe AI-based hardware and software solution for the AV market under the DRIVE brand, which includes the GPU-based hardware required to train the neural networks before their in-vehicle deployment, as well as to re-simulate their operation.

What is included in the company's sales and marketing strategy?|Working with end customers and industry ecosystems globally through a partner network that includes OEMs, ODMs, and various suppliers.|Our worldwide sales and marketing strategy is key to achieving our objective of providing markets with our high-performance and efficient GPU and embedded system-on-a-chip, or SOC, platforms. Our sales and marketing teams, located across our global markets, work closely with end customers in each industry.

Who in the company is responsible for assisting the partner network in designing system designs that incorporate company platforms?|A team of application engineers is responsible for assisting the partner network in designing system designs that incorporate company platforms.|We also employ a team of application engineers to assist our partner network in designing, testing, and qualifying system designs that incorporate our platforms.

How does the company encourage the development of applications optimized for its GPUs?|The company encourages the development of applications optimized for its GPUs by establishing strong relationships with the software development community and making its products available to developers prior to launch.|To encourage the development of applications optimized for our GPUs, we seek to establish and maintain strong relationships in the software development community. Our developer program makes our products available to developers prior to launch.

What training does the company's Deep Learning Institute provide?|The Deep Learning Institute provides in-person and online training for developers to build AI and accelerated computing applications that leverage the company’s GPU and CUDA platforms.|Our Deep Learning Institute provides in-person and online training for developers in industries and organizations around the world to build AI and accelerated computing applications that leverage our GPU and CUDA platforms.

How has the company's business evolved over time?|The company's business has evolved from focusing primarily on gaming products to broader markets, and from chips to platforms and complete systems.|As NVIDIA’s business has evolved from a focus primarily on gaming products to broader markets, and from chips to platforms and complete systems, so, too, have our avenues to market.

Sales to Dell Technologies Inc. accounted for 11% of the company's total revenue for fiscal year 2020.|Sales to Dell Technologies Inc. accounted for 11% of the company's total revenue for fiscal year 2020.|Sales to Dell Technologies Inc., or Dell, accounted for 11% of our total revenue for fiscal year 2020.

What is the company's manufacturing strategy for its semiconductor products?|The company utilizes a fabless manufacturing strategy, employing world-class suppliers for all phases of the manufacturing process, including wafer fabrication, assembly, testing, and packaging.|We do not directly manufacture semiconductors used for our products. Instead, we utilize a fabless manufacturing strategy, whereby we employ world-class suppliers for all phases of the manufacturing process, including wafer fabrication, assembly, testing, and packaging.

Which companies does the company utilize for wafer production?|The company utilizes Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited and Samsung Electronics Co. Ltd for wafer production.|We utilize industry-leading suppliers, such as Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited and Samsung Electronics Co. Ltd, to produce our semiconductor wafers.

What are some of the companies used as contract manufacturers and ODMs?|BYD, Hon Hai Precision Industry Co., Quanta Computer, and Wistron Corporation.|We also utilize industry-leading contract manufacturers, or CMs, such as BYD and Hon Hai Precision Industry Co., and ODMs such as Quanta Computer and Wistron Corporation, to manufacture some of our products for sale directly to end customers.

How did the company's cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities change at the end of fiscal year 2020?|They increased by 47% to $10.90 billion compared with the end of fiscal year 2019.|Our existing cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities balances increased by 47% to $10.90 billion at the end of fiscal year 2020 compared with the end of fiscal year 2019.

What strategies does the company use to manage its inventories?|The company manages inventories by communicating with customers and partners, forecasting demand, placing manufacturing orders based on demand, and maintaining substantial inventories as semi-finished products to balance customer demands.|We focus considerable attention on managing our inventories and other working-capital-related items. We manage inventories by communicating with our customers and partners and then using our industry experience to forecast demand on a platform-by-platform basis. We then place manufacturing orders for our products that are based on forecasted demand. We generally maintain substantial inventories of our products. A substantial amount of our inventories is maintained as semi-finished products that can be leveraged across a wide range of our processors to balance our customer demands.

What factors are believed to be principal competitive elements in the market for the company's products?|Principal competitive factors include performance, breadth of product offerings, access to customers and partners and distribution channels, software support, conformity to industry standard APIs, manufacturing capabilities, processor pricing, and total system costs.|We believe that the principal competitive factors in this market are performance, breadth of product offerings, access to customers and partners and distribution channels, software support, conformity to industry standard APIs, manufacturing capabilities, processor pricing, and total system costs.

[Irrelevant]Which companies are current competitors of the company, and what products do they provide?|Current competitors include Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), Intel Corporation, Xilinx, Inc., Alphabet Inc., Ambarella, Inc., Broadcom Inc., Qualcomm Incorporated, Renesas Electronics Corporation, Samsung, and Tesla Motors, providing discrete and integrated GPUs, SoC products, and chips for HPC and accelerated computing.|Our current competitors include:  • suppliers and licensors designing discrete and integrated GPUs and other accelerated computing solutions, including chipsets that incorporate 3D graphics, or HPC, such as Advanced Micro Devices, or AMD, Intel Corporation, or Intel, and Xilinx, Inc.;   • large internet services companies with internal teams designing chips that incorporates HPC or accelerated computing functionality as part of their internal solutions or platforms, such as Alphabet Inc.; and   • suppliers of SoC products that are embedded into automobiles, autonomous machines, and gaming devices, such as Ambarella, Inc., AMD, Broadcom Inc., Intel, Qualcomm Incorporated, Renesas Electronics Corporation, Samsung, and Xilinx, Inc. or companies with internal teams designing SoC products for internal use, such as Tesla Motors.

How does the company protect its intellectual property?|The company relies on a combination of patents, trademarks, trade secrets, nondisclosure agreements, and licensing arrangements. It also relies on international treaties, organizations, and foreign laws for protection.|We rely primarily on a combination of patents, trademarks, trade secrets, employee and third-party nondisclosure agreements, and licensing arrangements to protect our intellectual property in the United States and internationally. We also rely on international treaties, organizations, and foreign laws to protect our intellectual property.

What makes the piracy of the company's technology and products more likely in certain foreign countries?|The laws of certain foreign countries may not protect products or intellectual property rights to the same extent as U.S. laws, making piracy more likely.|The laws of certain foreign countries in which our products are or may be manufactured or sold, including various countries in Asia, may not protect our products or intellectual property rights to the same extent as the laws of the United States. This decreased protection makes the possibility of piracy of our technology and products more likely.

What degrees does Ms. Shoquist hold?|A B.S. degree in Electrical Engineering from Kansas State University and a B.S. degree in Biology from Santa Clara University.|Ms. Shoquist holds a B.S. degree in Electrical Engineering from Kansas State University and a B.S. degree in Biology from Santa Clara University.

In what year did Timothy S. Teter join NVIDIA?|2017|Timothy S. Teter joined NVIDIA in 2017 as Senior Vice President, General Counsel and Secretary and became Executive Vice President, General Counsel and Secretary in February 2018.

What position did Timothy S. Teter hold at Cooley LLP before joining NVIDIA?|Partner|Prior to NVIDIA, Mr. Teter spent more than two decades at the law firm of Cooley LLP. He was most recently a partner at Cooley, where he focused on litigating patent and technology related matters.

What is the educational background of Timothy S. Teter?|A B.S. degree in Mechanical Engineering from the University of California at Davis and a J.D. degree from Stanford Law School.|Mr. Teter holds a B.S. degree in Mechanical Engineering from the University of California at Davis and a J.D. degree from Stanford Law School.

Where can NVIDIA’s reports filed under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 be accessed for free?|On NVIDIA's website, http://www.nvidia.com, as soon as reasonably practicable after filing with the SEC.|Our annual reports on Form 10-K, quarterly reports on Form 10-Q, current reports on Form 8-K and, if applicable, amendments to those reports filed or furnished pursuant to Section 13(a) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended, are available free of charge on or through our web site, http://www.nvidia.com, as soon as reasonably practicable after we electronically file such material with, or furnish it to, the Securities and Exchange Commission, or the SEC.

What type of matters did Timothy S. Teter focus on at Cooley LLP?|Litigating patent and technology-related matters.|He was most recently a partner at Cooley, where he focused on litigating patent and technology related matters.

[Irrelevant]What information about NVIDIA is not considered part of their Annual Report on Form 10-K?|The information on their website or connected to it is not considered part of the Annual Report on Form 10-K.|Our web site and the information on it or connected to it are not a part of this Annual Report on Form 10-K.

What markets does NVIDIA's GPU-based visual and accelerated computing platforms target?|Gaming, Professional Visualization, Data Center, and Automotive|We created GPU-based visual and accelerated computing platforms that address four large markets: Gaming, Professional Visualization, Data Center, and Automotive.

How might competition affect NVIDIA's revenue in their target markets?|Competition may prevent revenue growth as competitors might offer less costly or superior products and services, leading to lower-than-expected selling prices and decreased demand for NVIDIA's offerings, negatively affecting revenue and operations.|Our target markets remain extremely competitive, and we expect competition to intensify as current competitors expand their product and/or service offerings, industry standards continue to evolve, customer needs change and new competitors enter these markets... If we are unable to successfully compete in our target markets... demand for our products, services and technologies could decrease, which would cause our revenue to decline and cause our results of operations to suffer.

What risks are associated with NVIDIA's research and development investments?|The risks include the possibility that these investments may not lead to significant revenue for several years, if at all, and may not result in products and technologies that are widely adopted.|Additionally, we continue to make considerable investments in research and development, which may not produce significant revenue for several years, if at all. If our investments are unsuccessful and we fail to develop new products, services and technologies, or if we focus on technologies that do not become widely adopted, our business, revenue, financial condition and results of operations could be adversely affected.

Why is it important for NVIDIA to anticipate changing needs and technology trends in their target markets?|Failing to anticipate and adapt to changing needs and technology trends might result in missed market opportunities, harming NVIDIA's business.|If we fail to anticipate the changing needs of our target markets and emerging technology trends, or if we do not appropriately adapt that strategy as market conditions evolve, in a timely manner to exploit potential market opportunities, our business will be harmed.

What are some potential challenges NVIDIA faces with system security and data protection?|NVIDIA faces challenges such as prevalent and sophisticated security breaches, malware, phishing, and cyber-attacks that threaten to disrupt operations, reduce expected revenue, increase expenses, damage their reputation, and adversely affect stock price.|System security and data protection breaches, as well as cyber-attacks, could disrupt our operations, reduce our expected revenue and increase our expenses, which could adversely affect our stock price and damage our reputation. Security breaches, computer malware, phishing, and cyber-attacks have become more prevalent and sophisticated in recent years.

How does the competitive landscape and consolidation trend in NVIDIA's target markets affect the company?|The trend towards consolidation could lead to fewer customers, partners, or suppliers, potentially negatively impacting NVIDIA's financial results.|In addition, the competitive landscape in our target markets has changed and may continue to evolve due to a trend toward consolidation, which could lead to fewer customers, partners, or suppliers, any of which could negatively affect our financial results.

What is necessary for NVIDIA to succeed in developing products for new markets like automotive and data center?|Considerable technical, financial, compliance, sales, and marketing investments are necessary, along with developing infrastructure like customer service and support, and meeting customer safety and compliance standards.|Such activities may require considerable technical, financial, compliance, sales and marketing investments. We devote significant resources to the development of technologies and business offerings in markets where we have a limited operating history, such as the automotive and data center markets, which presents additional risks to our business. We must also continue to develop the infrastructure needed to scale our business in these areas, including customer service and support. We also must meet customer safety and compliance standards.

What types of malicious software programs can hackers develop and deploy to exploit vulnerabilities in products?|Hackers may develop and deploy viruses, worms, and other malicious software programs that attack or exploit security vulnerabilities.|These hackers may also develop and deploy viruses, worms and other malicious software programs that attack or otherwise exploit security vulnerabilities in our products, including consumer and automotive products, where we utilize over-the-air updates to improve functionality over time.

Why might an organization's expenses increase due to security threats?|Expenses may increase due to the need to continuously engineer more secure products and enhance security and reliability features.|To defend against security threats, both to our internal systems and those of our customers, we must continuously engineer more secure products and enhance security and reliability features, which may result in increased expenses.

What could happen if a security breach results in the loss or misuse of sensitive data?|A security breach could result in litigation, potential liability, paying damages, regulatory inquiries or actions, damage to the brand and reputation, or other harm to the business.|Actual or perceived breaches of our security measures or the accidental loss, inadvertent disclosure or unapproved dissemination of proprietary information or sensitive or confidential data about us, our partners, our customers or third parties could expose us and the parties affected to a risk of loss or misuse of this information, resulting in litigation and potential liability, paying damages, regulatory inquiries or actions, damage to our brand and reputation or other harm to our business.

How might interruptions in service due to security disruptions affect a company?|Interruptions in service could lead to delays, cessation of service, loss of customers, and could negatively impact financial results, stock price, and reputation.|We may experience interruptions, delays, cessation of service and loss of existing or potential customers. Such disruptions could adversely impact our ability to fulfill orders and interrupt other critical functions. Delayed sales, lower margins or lost customers as a result of these disruptions could adversely affect our financial results, stock price and reputation.

What are some risks associated with relying on third-party foundries for wafer manufacturing?|Risks include a lack of guaranteed supply, higher component prices due to supply constraints, failure to procure raw materials, and inadequate manufacturing capacity.|We do not manufacture the silicon wafers used for our GPUs and Tegra processors and do not own or operate a wafer fabrication facility. Instead, we are dependent on industry-leading foundries, such as Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited and Samsung Electronics Co. Ltd., to manufacture our semiconductor wafers using their fabrication equipment and techniques. As a result, we face several significant risks which could have an adverse effect on our ability to meet customer demand and/or negatively impact our business operations, gross margin, revenue and/or financial results, including: • | a lack of guaranteed supply of wafers and other components and potential higher wafer and component prices due to supply constraints; • | a failure by our foundries to procure raw materials or to provide or allocate adequate or any manufacturing or test capacity for our products.

Why might low manufacturing yields pose a problem for a company?|Low manufacturing yields can affect customer demand, increase manufacturing costs, harm relationships, and negatively impact business operations and financial results.|In addition, low manufacturing yields could have an adverse effect on our ability to meet customer demand, increase manufacturing costs, harm customer or partner relationships, and/or negatively impact our business operations, gross margin, revenue and/or financial results.

What are the possible reasons for low manufacturing yields according to the content?|Low manufacturing yields may result from product design or process technology failure, and problems may not be identified until well into the manufacturing process.|Manufacturing yields for our products are a function of product design, which is developed largely by us, and process technology, which typically is proprietary to the foundry. Low yields may result from either product design or process technology failure. We do not know whether a yield problem will exist until our design is actually manufactured by the foundry. As a result, yield problems may not be identified until well into the manufacturing process and require us and the foundry to cooperate to resolve the problem.

What types of disruptions could harm the business and lead to significant losses?|Natural or man-made disasters such as floods, fires, extreme weather, cyber-attacks, terrorist attacks, medical epidemics or pandemics, catastrophic events, or climate change.|The occurrence of any of these disruptions could harm our business and result in significant losses, a decline in revenue and an increase in our costs and expenses. These disruptions include natural or man-made disasters like floods, fires, extreme weather, cyber-attacks, terrorist attacks, medical epidemics or pandemics, catastrophic events, or climate change.

Where are the corporate headquarters and a portion of the company's research and development activities located?|California|Our corporate headquarters, and a portion of our research and development activities, are located in California.

What geographical locations are mentioned as critical for business operations and supply chain?|California, Taiwan, China, Hong Kong, Korea|Other critical business operations, finished goods inventory, and some of our suppliers are located in Asia, including Taiwan, China, Hong Kong, and Korea. A large portion of our data center capacity is in California.

What impact could geopolitical changes or changes in government regulations have on the company?|They could result in changing regulatory requirements, trade policies, import duties, and economic disruptions affecting operating strategies, product demand, access to global markets, hiring, and profitability.|Geopolitical change or changes in government regulations and policies may result in changing regulatory requirements, trade policies, import duties and economic disruptions that could impact our operating strategies, product demand, access to global markets, hiring, and profitability.

What event in January 2020 is mentioned, and what impact did it have?|A novel strain of coronavirus identified in China, leading to manufacturing shutdowns, commerce disruptions, and global travel restrictions.|In January 2020, a novel strain of coronavirus was identified in China, resulting in shutdowns of manufacturing and commerce, as well as global travel restrictions to contain the virus.

What could happen if the company fails to estimate customer demand properly?|Their financial results could be harmed due to excess or obsolete inventory.|If we fail to estimate customer demand properly, our financial results could be harmed. Situations that may result in excess or obsolete inventory include changes in market conditions and demand for products.

What are some factors that might lead to excess or obsolete inventory?|Changes in business conditions, changes in market conditions, a decrease in product demand, inventory obsolescence due to rapidly changing technology, introduction of new products, less demand for new products, and increased competition.|Situations that may result in excess or obsolete inventory include changes in business conditions, changes in market conditions, a decrease in product demand, inventory obsolescence due to rapidly changing technology, introduction of new products, less demand for new products, and increased competition.

What are some reasons for potential obsolescence of products in the technology industry?|Rapidly changing technology, shifting customer requirements, introduction of new products leading to lower demand for older products, less demand than expected for newly-introduced products, and increased competition, including competitive pricing actions.|Obsolescence can occur due to rapidly changing technology or customer requirements; the introduction of new products can result in lower demand for older products; there can be less demand than expected for newly-introduced products; and there may be increased competition, including competitive pricing actions.

What impact can the cancellation or deferral of customer purchase orders have on a company's inventory?|The cancellation or deferral of customer purchase orders can result in a company holding excess inventory, which could adversely affect its gross margins.|The cancellation or deferral of customer purchase orders could result in our holding excess inventory, which could adversely affect our gross margins.

Why might a company be required to write down its inventory or experience a reduction in average selling prices?|If a company incorrectly forecasts product demand, it may need to write down inventory to the lower of cost or market value, or write-off excess inventory, leading to a reduction in average selling prices.|We could be required to write-down our inventory to the lower of cost or market or write-off excess inventory, and we could experience a reduction in average selling prices if we incorrectly forecast product demand.

What challenges might a company face if it underestimates customer demand for its products?|If a company underestimates customer demand, its foundry partners may lack the lead-time or capacity to increase production, causing insufficient inventory to fulfill customer orders promptly.|If we underestimate our customers' demand for our products, our foundry partners may not have adequate lead-time or capacity to increase production and we may not be able to obtain sufficient inventory to fill customers' orders on a timely basis.

Failing to fulfill orders on a timely basis could damage customer relationships, result in loss of revenue and market share, and harm the company's reputation.|If we fail to fulfill our customers' orders on a timely basis, or at all, our customer relationships could be damaged, we could lose revenue and market share and our reputation could be damaged.

What portion of a company's total revenue did sales to Dell account for in fiscal year 2020?|11% of the company's total revenue in fiscal year 2020 came from sales to Dell.|For fiscal year 2020, 11% of our total revenue was from one customer, Dell.

What percentage of a company's revenue in fiscal year 2020 was generated from sales outside the United States?|92% of the company's total revenue for fiscal year 2020 was from sales outside the United States.|Revenue from sales outside of the United States accounted for 92% of total revenue for fiscal year 2020.

What percentage of the employees were located outside of the United States as of January 26, 2020?|Approximately 46%|As of January 26, 2020, approximately 46% of our employees were located outside of the United States.

What impact could unexpected changes in legislative or regulatory requirements have on a business?|Unexpected changes in legislative or regulatory requirements could have a material adverse effect on a business's financial condition and results of operations.|Unexpected changes in, or impositions of, legislative or regulatory requirements, including changes in tax laws, can have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations.
